title: Maareecha turns into Golden Deer
introduction: On travelling by the aircraft like chariot Ravana and Maareecha enter Dandaka forest and arrive at the threshold of Rama's hermitage. Then at the insistence of Ravana Maareecha assumes the form of an amazing golden Deer, and Seetha catches a sight of that deer.
closing: The vāstu śāstra or the Ancient Indian Architecture lays down certain parameters for Towns, cities etc. Of them the township is said to be aneka nārī sambaddham nanā śilpi janaiḥ vṛtam | kraya vikrayaiḥ kīrṇam sarva devaiḥ samanvitam nagaram tu iti vikhyātam adored with many ladies, many sculptors or architects, and with many deities, and where the buying and selling goes on it is nagaram the township.

The Seaports are said as: pattanam śṛṇu sāmpratam | dvīpāntara gata dravya kraya vikrayikaiḥ yutam | pattanam tu abdhi tīre syāt | one which has all the above aspects but which is at seaside, it is pattanam seaport. The township between a nagara and puram is kharvaṭam

And the City is: kraya vikrayaiḥ yutam nānā jāti samanvitam | tantuvāya samāyuktam tat puram tu vikathyateThe one with all the above aspects plus very many civilisations and weavers and the like craftsmen, is purī, the city. Apart from these, the royal places, army stations etc., do comprise the ten varieties of urban places as said in the above verse, where the village is the first unit.
इति वाल्मीकि रामायणे आदि काव्ये अरण्य काण्डे द्वि चत्वारिंशः सर्गः
Thus, this is the 42nd chapter in Aranya Kanda of Valmiki Ramayana, the First Epic poem of India.

verses.devanagari:
एवम् उक्त्वा तु परुषम् मारीचो रावणम् ततः |
गच्छावः इति अब्रवीत् दीनो भयात् रात्रिम् चर प्रभोः
verses.iast:
evam uktvā tu paruṣam mārīco rāvaṇam tataḥ |
gacchāvaḥ iti abravīt dīno bhayāt rātrim cara prabhoḥ
verses.translation: Maareecha though curtly said in that way, then afraid of the king of night-walkers he became self-pitying, and said to Ravana, 'let us go.'

glosses.meaning: Maareecha, in this way, curtly, said, but

verses.devanagari:
दृष्टाः च अहम् पुनः तेन शर चाप असि धारिणा |
मद्वधो उद्यत शस्त्रेण विनष्टम् जीवितम् च मे
verses.iast:
dṛṣṭāḥ ca aham punaḥ tena śara cāpa asi dhāriṇā |
madvadho udyata śastreṇa vinaṣṭam jīvitam ca me
verses.translation: "If he who wields a bow, arrows and a sword, and who brandishes a weapon to only kill me happens to see me again, deem my life is verily lost, without his shooting any arrow.

glosses.meaning: arrow, bow, sword, by the wielder of
for my, killing, [if he with] upraised, [his] weapon

verses.devanagari:
न हि रामम् पराक्रम्य जीवन् प्रति निवर्तते |
वर्तते प्रति रूपो असौ यम दण्ड हतस्य ते
verses.iast:
na hi rāmam parākramya jīvan prati nivartate |
var.htate prati rūpo asau yama daṇḍa hatasya te
verses.translation: "None can really make so bold at Rama to reappear with life, isn't it. What is appearing before you is the reflected image of mine, as I am already slain by the wand of Yama, the Terminator, the moment I conceded to your demand.

glosses.meaning: at Rama, to affront - make so bold
by Yama [ the Terminator,] with wand, slain

verses.devanagari:
किम् नु कर्तुम् मया शक्यम् एवम् त्वयि दुरात्मनि |
एष गच्छामि अहम् तात स्वस्ति ते अस्तु निशाचरः
verses.iast:
kim nu kartum mayā śakyam evam tvayi durātmani |
eṣa gacchāmi aham tāta svasti te astu niśācaraḥ
verses.translation: "When you are spiteful, oh, boy, indeed what can I possibly do otherwise, oh, night-walker, thither I go, may good betide you." So said Maareecha to Ravana.

glosses.meaning: by me, what is, possible, to do, indeed

verses.devanagari:
प्रहृष्टः तु अभवत् तेन वचनेन स राक्षसः |
परिष्वज्य सुसंश्लिष्टम् इदम् वचनम् अब्रवीत्
verses.iast:
prahṛṣṭaḥ tu abhavat tena vacanena sa rākṣasaḥ |
pariṣvajya susaṃśliṣṭam idam vacanam abravīt
verses.translation: By that word of Maareecha demon Ravana is very much gladdened and he spoke this sentence tightly hugging him.

verses.devanagari:
एतत् शौण्डीर्य - चौत्तिर्य -न्युक्तम् ते मत् च्छंद वश वर्तिनः |
इदानीम् असि मारीचः पूर्वम् अन्यो निशाचरः
verses.iast:
etat śauṇḍīrya - cauttirya -nyuktam te mat cchaṃda vaśa vartinaḥ |
idānīm asi mārīcaḥ pūrvam anyo niśācaraḥ
verses.translation: "This word of yours shows your obduracy for you are abiding under the control of my dictate, and though you were a different night-walker earlier, henceforth you are really the good old Maareecha.
notes: Some mms use the word śauṇḍīryafor cchauṭirya, where śauṇḍīryais the word for courageousness, śauṇḍīrya tyāgī vīrayoḥ : nighanṭu The other way to tell this is: "Though your words show the fear of my dictate, but on listening those obdurate words, it appears that you have spoken them for yourself, regaining the grit of your demon-hood and estimating Rama as your own enemy," by which Ravana is shirking his responsibility to Maareecha himself in the event of the death of Maareecha.

verses.devanagari:
आरुह्यताम् शीघ्रम् खगो रत्न विभूषितः |
मया सह रथो युक्तः पिशाच वदनैः खरैः
verses.iast:
āruhyatām śīghram khago ratna vibhūṣitaḥ |
mayā saha ratho yuktaḥ piśāca vadanaiḥ kharaiḥ
verses.translation: "Then you promptly emplane this sky-flying chariot which is yoked with ghost-faced mules and adorned with gems along with me.
notes: It may be noted that this sort of air-chariots, though richly decorated with valuable gold and gems, but drawn by asses or mules, that too ghost-faced ones, are a kind of the then sci-fi version of aircrafts. Ravana's son Indrajit also uses such spaceships in Yuddha Kanda and his weaponry is altogether different, i.e., somewhat like the present day laser oriented hardware. These propellers may not be construed as real donkeys or mules but some powered vehicle-drawing instruments designed to look like ordinary harmless creatures.

glosses.meaning: with ghost, faced ones, asses - mules, yoked with
promptly, me, along with, you emplane.

verses.devanagari:
प्रलोभयित्वा वैदेहीम् यथा इष्टम् गन्तुम् अर्हसि |
ताम् शून्ये प्रसभम् सीताम् आनयिष्यामि मैथिलीम्
verses.iast:
pralobhayitvā vaidehīm yathā iṣṭam gantum arhasi |
tām śūnye prasabham sītām ānayiṣyāmi maithilīm
verses.translation: "On deluding Vaidehi it is apt of you to go as you please, and I will bring that Seetha of Mithila, however defiant it might be." Thus Ravana said to Maareecha.
notes: Ravana is saying repeatedly that Maareecha can go away after beguiling Seetha and misleading Rama and Lakshmana away from hermitage. Maareecha knows that there is no place to go away from Rama's arrow, which once chased him up to seashore. But Ravana presumes that if Maareecha is capable enough, he will escape Rama, or if this old demon Maareecha is incapable of it, he may perhaps die by the arrow of Rama, for which Ravana is unconcerned.

glosses.meaning: as, you please, to go, apt of you
in empty place - devoid of people
one from Mithila, her, Seetha will be

verses.devanagari:
तथा इति उवाच एनम् रावणम् ताटका सुतः |
ततो रावण मारीचौ विमानम् इव तम् रथम्
आरुह्य ययतुः शीघ्रम् तस्मात् आश्रम मण्डलात् |
verses.iast:
tathā iti uvāca enam rāvaṇam tāṭakā sutaḥ |
tato rāvaṇa mārīcau vimānam iva tam ratham
āruhya yayatuḥ śīghram tasmāt āśrama maṇḍalāt |
verses.translation: Tataka's son Maareecha said "All right" to Ravana, and then both Ravana and Maareecha mounted the chariot as they would emplane an aircraft and swiftly journeyed from the surroundings of Maareecha's hermitage.

glosses.meaning: from that, hermitage's, surroundings - from Maareecha's hermitage

verses.devanagari:
तथैव तत्र पश्यन्तौ पत्तनानि वनानि च
गिरीम् च सरिताः सर्वा राष्ट्राणि नगराणि च |
verses.iast:
tathaiva tatra paśyantau pattanāni vanāni ca
girīm ca saritāḥ sarvā rāṣṭrāṇi nagarāṇi ca |
verses.translation: While looking at the seaports and forests, also at all the mountains and rivers, even at the cities and provinces en route they proceeded.

glosses.meaning: mountains, also, rivers, all of them

verses.devanagari:
समेत्य दण्डक अरण्यम् राघवस्य आश्रमम् ततः
ददर्श सह मरीचो रावणो राक्षसाधिपः |
verses.iast:
sametya daṇḍaka araṇyam rāghavasya āśramam tataḥ
dadarśa saha marīco rāvaṇo rākṣasādhipaḥ |
verses.translation: On reaching Dandaka forest along with Maareecha the king of demons Ravana has then seen the hermitage of Raghava.
notes: Please refer to the endnote for the Ancient Indian way of classification of villages, towns, and cities as per Indian architecture called vāstu śāstra.

verses.devanagari:
अवतीर्य रथात् तस्मात् ततः कांचन भूषणात्
हस्ते गृहीत्वा मारीचम् रावणो वाक्यम् अब्रवीत् |
verses.iast:
avatīrya rathāt tasmāt tataḥ kāṃcana bhūṣaṇāt
haste gṛhītvā mārīcam rāvaṇo vākyam abravīt |
verses.translation: Alighting the chariot that is decorated with golden ornaments Ravana then spoke this sentence to Maareecha taking his hand into his.

glosses.meaning: with golden [ornaments,] decorated, from that, chariot, having alighted

verses.devanagari:
एतत् राम आश्रम पदम् दृश्यते कदली वृतम्
क्रियताम् तत् सखे शीघ्रम् यत् अर्थम् वयम् आगताः |
verses.iast:
etat rāma āśrama padam dṛśyate kadalī vṛtam
kriyatām tat sakhe śīghram yat artham vayam āgatāḥ |
verses.translation: "This one which we are seeing and which is surrounded with banana plants is the threshold of Rama's hermitage, and -`----oh, friend, the purpose for which we came here let it be effectuated promptly." Thus Ravana hastened Maareecha.

glosses.meaning: we, for which, reason, came here

verses.devanagari:
स रावण वचः श्रुत्वा मारीचो राक्षसः तदा
मृगो भूत्वा आश्रम द्वारि रामस्य विचचार ह |
verses.iast:
sa rāvaṇa vacaḥ śrutvā mārīco rākṣasaḥ tadā
mṛgo bhūtvā āśrama dvāri rāmasya vicacāra ha |
verses.translation: "And on hearing Ravana's words demon Maareecha then became a deer and indeed ambled freely in the frontage of Rama's hermitage.

verses.devanagari:
स तु रूपम् समास्थाय महत् अद्भुत दर्शनम्
मणिप्रवर शृंगाग्रः सित असित मुखाकृतिः |
verses.iast:
sa tu rūpam samāsthāya mahat adbhuta darśanam
maṇipravara śṛṃgāgraḥ sita asita mukhākṛtiḥ |
verses.translation: Adopting the form of a gorgeous deer which is superbly amazing just by its appearance, whose tips of antlers are in the hue of best sapphires, and whose face is whitish at some places and not so whitish at other in its look, he became a Golden Deer and moved thereabout.

glosses.meaning: sapphire blue [in the hue of,] the best, horn, with tips
whitish, not, so whitish, face's, in look
deer, on becoming, he moved about.

verses.devanagari:
रक्तपद्मोत्पल मुख इन्द्रनीलोत्पल श्रवाः
किंचित् अभ्युन्नत ग्रीव इन्द्रनील निभ उदरः |
verses.iast:
raktapadmotpala mukha indranīlotpala śravāḥ
kiṃcit abhyunnata grīva indranīla nibha udaraḥ |
verses.translation: One of its cheeks in the shade of a reddish-lotus while the other in the hue of a bluish-lotus, one of its ears is in the hue of bloomed blue-lotus while the other is in the shade of a sapphire, while the shine of its stomach is like that of a best blue-diamond, Indra-niila-maNi, and with a little upraised neck that deer has moved about there.

glosses.meaning: red, lotus [on one side,] blue lotus, [on the other,] face [cheeks]
Indra, Blue [sapphirine in hue,] [bloomed] blue-lotus like, ears
Indra, blue diamond, in shine, stomach, [lower lip]

verses.devanagari:
मधूक निभ पार्श्वः च कंज किंजल्क सम्निभः
वैदूर्य संकाश खुरः तनु जंघः सुसंहतः |
verses.iast:
madhūka nibha pārśvaḥ ca kaṃja kiṃjalka samnibhaḥ
vaidūrya saṃkāśa khuraḥ tanu jaṃghaḥ susaṃhataḥ |
verses.translation: One flank is shining whitish like Madhuka flowers and the other is similar to the roseate fibrils of lotuses, while its hooves are similar to the gemstone lapis, calves thin, and thus with very well cohered limbs that deer moved about there.

glosses.meaning: Mahuka flower [whitish flower from which country liquor is prepared,] in shine

verses.devanagari:
इन्द्र आयुध सवर्णेन पुच्छेन ऊर्ध्वम् विराजितः
मनोहर स्निग्ध वर्णो रत्नैः नाना विधैः वृतः |
verses.iast:
indra āyudha savarṇena pucchena ūrdhvam virājitaḥ
manohara snigdha varṇo ratnaiḥ nānā vidhaiḥ vṛtaḥ |
verses.translation: With an upraised tail that shone forth in a tinge equal to the weapon of Indra, namely Rainbow, and with a complexion that is lustrous and dappled with many diverse gemlike dapples, that deer moved thereabout with a heart-stealing aura.

glosses.meaning: to up - upraised [tail,] verily shining forth
many, diverse ones, with gems [gemlike dapples,] encompassed [dappled with.]

verses.devanagari:
क्षणेन राक्षसो जातो मृगः परम शोभनः
वनम् प्रज्वलयन् रम्यम् राम आश्रम पदम् च तत् |
verses.iast:
kṣaṇena rākṣaso jāto mṛgaḥ parama śobhanaḥ
vanam prajvalayan ramyam rāma āśrama padam ca tat |
verses.translation: Thus that demon Maareecha emerged like a highly splendorous and fascinating deer in a wink highly irradiating those woodlands, and the threshold of Rama's hermitage in particular.

verses.devanagari:
मनोहरम् दर्शनीयम् रूपम् कृत्वा स राक्षसः
प्रलोभनार्थम् वैदेह्या नाना धातु विचित्रितम् |
विचरन् गच्छते सम्यक् शाद्वलानि समंततः
verses.iast:
manoharam darśanīyam rūpam kṛtvā sa rākṣasaḥ
pralobhanārtham vaidehyā nānā dhātu vicitritam |
vicaran gacchate samyak śādvalāni samaṃtataḥ
verses.translation: Adopting such an exquisite and heart-stealing form which is amazingly dappled with the colours of diverse ores, that demon ambled all over there freely with the bearing of a real deer in order that Vaidehi might be deluded, and he moved forward onto the pastures.

glosses.meaning: various, ores, [colours of ores,] amazingly, [body] painted with

verses.devanagari:
रोप्यैः बिन्दु शतैः चित्रो भूत्वा च प्रिय दर्शनः |
विटपीनाम् किसलयान् भक्षयन् विचचार ह
verses.iast:
ropyaiḥ bindu śataiḥ citro bhūtvā ca priya darśanaḥ |
viṭapīnām kisalayān bhakśayan vicacāra ha
verses.translation: And with hundreds of silvery stipples of body he became an astonishing deer with pleasant looks and indeed moved chewing new grass-blades of trees.

glosses.meaning: with silvery, stipples [of body,] hundreds of
of trees, new grass-blades, to graze

verses.devanagari:
कदली गृहकम् गत्वा कर्णिकारानि ततः ततः |
समाश्रयन् मंदगतिः सीता संदर्शनम् ततः
verses.iast:
kadalī gṛhakam gatvā karṇikārāni tataḥ tataḥ |
samāśrayan maṃdagatiḥ sītā saṃdarśanam tataḥ
verses.translation: That Golden Deer has gone into the boscages of banana plants, and moved here and there around Karnikara trees, and then resorted to a place which is within the eyeshot of Seetha.

glosses.meaning: field of view - at such a place
well, abided - resorted to such a place.

verses.devanagari:
राजीव चित्र पृष्ठः स विरराज महामृगः |
राम आश्रम पद अभ्याशे विचचार यथा सुखम्
verses.iast:
rājīva citra pṛṣṭhaḥ sa virarāja mahāmṛgaḥ |
rāma āśrama pada abhyāśe vicacāra yathā sukham
verses.translation: With an odd lotus like hind-side that astounding deer is verily scintillating, and it milled around the surroundings in the threshold of Rama's hermitage according to its own delight.

verses.devanagari:
पुनर् गत्वा निवृत्तः च विचचार मृगोत्तमः |
गत्वा मुहूर्तम् त्वरया पुनः प्रति निवर्तते
verses.iast:
punar gatvā nivṛttaḥ ca vicacāra mṛgottamaḥ |
gatvā muhūrtam tvarayā punaḥ prati nivartate
verses.translation: That excellent deer beats a retreat and again returns, and meanders thus time and again, and turns its tail for sometime only to return once again very playfully.

glosses.meaning: on going away, again, on coming back, also

verses.devanagari:
विक्रीडन् च पुनर् भूमौ पुनर् एव निषीदति |
आश्रम द्वारम् आगम्य मृग यूथानि गच्छति
verses.iast:
vikrīḍan ca punar bhūmau punar eva niṣīdati |
āśrama dvāram āgamya mṛga yūthāni gacchati
verses.translation: Again gambolling everywhere it sits somewhere on the ground, then, on coming to the threshold of hermitage it goes towards herds of deer.

glosses.meaning: on ground, again, thus, sinks down - sits down

verses.devanagari:
मृग यूथैः अनुगतः पुनर् एव निवर्तते |
सीता दर्शनम् आकांक्षन् राक्षसो मृगताम् गतः
परिभ्रमति चित्राणि मण्डलानि विनिष्पतन् |
verses.iast:
mṛga yūthaiḥ anugataḥ punar eva nivar.htate |
sītā darśanam ākāṃkṣan rākṣaso mṛgatām gataḥ
paribhramati citrāṇi maṇḍalāni viniṣpatan |
verses.translation: That demon who has gone into the deer-hood has gone after some herd of deer. But he returned again though that herd followed him wanting to fraternise, in order that he shall remain perceptible to Seetha, and he whirligiged in amusing circles while leaping and bounding to and from that herd of deer.

glosses.meaning: deer-hood, on going into, demon - Maareecha
to Seetha, to be perceptible, desirous of
by deer, by herds, when followed [fraternizing]
verily, out, falling - leaping and bounding

verses.devanagari:
समुद्वीक्ष्य च सर्वे तम् मृगा ये अन्ये वनेचराः
उपगम्य समाघ्राय विद्रवन्ति दिशो दश |
verses.iast:
samudvīkṣya ca sarve tam mṛgā ye anye vanecarāḥ
upagamya samāghrāya vidravanti diśo daśa |
verses.translation: All the other animals moving in that forest on seeing this demon-deer with their necks up have come close to it, and on smelling it well they are running away to all the ten directions noticing it as a demon turned into a deer.
notes: Here the animals are portrayed as better beings than humans in identifying demons or ghosts. Though they may not know or wish to know about god, the apparent ghost scares them. Humans apperceive neither god nor ghost because they are half of each.

glosses.meaning: which, all, other, animals - are there

verses.devanagari:
राक्षसः सो अपि तान् वन्यान् मृगान् मृगवधे रतः
प्रच्छादनार्थम् भावस्य न भक्षयति संस्पृशन् |
verses.iast:
rākṣasaḥ so api tān vanyān mṛgān mṛgavadhe rataḥ
pracchādanārtham bhāvasya na bhakṣayati saṃspṛśan |
verses.translation: Even that demon in the deer's semblance Maareecha, though indulged in killing those forest animals, and though the other animals are touching him, he is not killing and eating them indulgently, only for the reason of camouflaging his present nature of demon-hood.

verses.devanagari:
तस्मिन् एव ततः काले वैदेही शुभलोचना
कुसुम अपचये व्यग्रा पादपान् अभ्यवर्तत |
verses.iast:
tasmin eva tataḥ kāle vaidehī śubhalocanā
kusuma apacaye vyagrā pādapān abhyavartata |
verses.translation: What is more, Vaidehi with her felicitous eyes came towards trees yearning for plucking the flowers in the same instant.

glosses.meaning: at that, only, at time - in the same instant

verses.devanagari:
कर्णिकारान् अशोकान् च चूताम् च मदिरेक्षणा
कुसुमानि अपचिन्वन्ती चचार रुचिरानना |
verses.iast:
karṇikārān aśokān ca cūtām ca madirekṣaṇā
kusumāni apacinvantī cacāra rucirānanā |
verses.translation: And she with her inebriating glances and delightful visage moved there about while plucking flowers of Karnikaara, Ashoka, and of Mango trees.

verses.devanagari:
अनर्हा अरण्य वासस्य सा तम् रत्नमयम् मृगम्
मुक्ता मणि विचित्र अंगम् ददर्श परम अंगना |
verses.iast:
anarhā araṇya vāsasya sā tam ratnamayam mṛgam
muktā maṇi vicitra aṃgam dadarśa parama aṃganā |
verses.translation: That select lady who is unmeet for forest life beheld that deer which is completely gemlike and whose limbs are surprising as though studded with pearls and gems.

glosses.meaning: [studded with] pearls, gems, surprising, having limbs

verses.devanagari:
तम् वै रुचिर दंत ओष्ठम् रूप्य धातु तनू रुहम्
विस्मयात् उत्फुल्ल नयना स स्नेहम् समुदैक्षत |
verses.iast:
tam vai rucira daṃta oṣṭham rūpya dhātu tanū ruham
vismayāt utphulla nayanā sa sneham samudaikṣata |
verses.translation: And she that Seetha goggled the Golden Deer with a wide-eyed astonishment, which deer has pretty lips and teeth, hair resembling silver and copper ores, and she indeed gazed at it with an affinity for wildlife.

glosses.meaning: one with pretty, teeth, lips - deer
silver, ore [like copper ore coloured,] body, born [hairs]
well, raising eyes, has seen - rubbernecked, goggled

verses.devanagari:
स च ताम् राम दयिताम् पश्यन् मायामयो मृगः
विचचार ततः तत्र दीपयन् इव तत् वनम् |
verses.iast:
sa ca tām rāma dayitām paśyan māyāmayo mṛgaḥ
vicacāra tataḥ tatra dīpayan iva tat vanam |
verses.translation: On seeing Rama's wife Seetha that highly phantasmal deer too then moved there about as though to scintillate that woodland.

glosses.meaning: at her, Rama's, wife, on seeing
that, woods, to scintillate, as though

verses.devanagari:
अदृष्ट पूर्वम् दृष्ट्वा तम् नाना रत्नमयम् मृगम् |
विस्मयम् परमम् सीता जगाम जनक आत्मजा
verses.iast:
adṛṣṭa pūrvam dṛṣṭvā tam nānā ratnamayam mṛgam |
vismayam paramam sītā jagāma janaka ātmajā
verses.translation: To see such a deer which is hitherto unseen, and which is as though studded with numerous gems, the daughter of Janaka, Seetha, went in to an intense wonderment. [3-42-35b, c]
notes: The stress continuously laid on the eyes of Seetha is observable, only to conclude that 'trust not vhat thy eyes śov you...'
